feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform leadership, with clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector positioning. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, and could sharpen impact by emphasizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in director-level leadership and then consulting; this supports credibility and seniority.  
- Strong domain fit: digital platforms, governance, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently reinforced across sections.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption improvements, campaign performance, or cost/time savings.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other phrasing, and mixed punctuation/list styles. “Ranked among the top public universities…” under Education feels unnecessary. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. Tightening it and foregrounding the most distinctive strengths will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider a sharper version: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems, governance models, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Delivers scalable editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve discovery, coordination, and audience engagement.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more outcome-oriented language like “modernizing enterprise web ecosystems” or “designing scalable digital systems.”
- Reduce the list length; keep 3–4 core themes only: web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, and AI-enabled experiences.
- Use parallel phrasing and consistent style: “web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, and AI-enabled experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Multimedia production” is already well covered in Work Experience and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize distinctive, high-value capabilities rather than restating broad areas already covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use sharper, outcome-oriented phrasing: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization,” and “Digital governance, editorial workflows & publishing systems” for more specificity.
- Group related items to reduce overlap and improve scanability: web/platforms, governance/operations, analytics/AI, and multimedia/advocacy.
- Replace broader phrases with more differentiated ones, e.g. “Cross-channel communications operations” or “Public-sector advocacy communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance, editorial workflows & publishing systems • Analytics, dashboards & reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search & content discovery • Workflow automation & platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production, livestreaming & studio operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with Topline Skills and Recent Projects.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also covered in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope will make it more distinctive and scannable.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise achievement-focused bullet rather than paragraph-style text.
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong, but simplify where possible and keep parallel structure across all four entries.
- Emphasize recency and specificity by anchoring projects to platform/type: “Drupal 10 campaign microsite,” “interactive conference display,” “recurring advocacy video series.”
- Where available, add light outcome language (for example, “to improve policy-content discovery” or “designed for ongoing campaign expansion”) without repeating full job-responsibility detail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite closely repeat current consultant bullets; shorten here or frame them as “selected projects” to avoid redundancy.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep this entry brief unless you can add a distinct result or scale detail.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics for coordinated cross-channel communications” instead of “Build and refine digital systems…”
- Consolidate web/CMS bullets: combine microsites, front-end implementation, and troubleshooting into one bullet focused on delivered platform improvements.
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, time saved, or stakeholder teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media; keep only if you can show a new consulting-specific result.
- Microsite and AI search details duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let Projects carry the feature detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be stronger if tightened around 3–4 signature outcomes and phrased to emphasize transformation, team leadership, and business impact over channel inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Combine web and analytics wins: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers; expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused: replace “reaching tens of thousands / thousands” with stronger metrics if available (open rates, engagement growth, campaign performance, production volume).
- Tighten studio/governance bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring multimedia content” and “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior Associate Communications Director role.
- Video expansion may duplicate older entries unless this bullet stresses the studio build and organizational-scale impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scope so it shows how this role built the foundation for the later director position.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Ran day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a repeatable policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams to improve alignment and publishing cadence.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and cross-team coordination.
- If possible, add metrics: open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround-time improvements, or audience growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; use “ran” or “managed” and emphasize execution rather than leadership.
- Video/newsletter language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this version focused on scaling and formalizing those channels.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen toward senior-level differentiators and use phrasing that reflects enterprise scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with tighter, higher-value wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for multi-publisher environments
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider adding scale where possible in adjacent experience instead of here; skills sections read better as concise capability signals, not pseudo-bullets.
- If you want this section to feel more distinctive, swap “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content operations and publishing standards” to better match your recent leadership work.
- Keep terminology consistent with the header/core competencies: use “governance,” “operations,” and “enterprise” rather than softer phrasing like “planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability-led, not inventory-led; lead with strategic strengths and keep only the most relevant platforms.
- Suggested rewrite: **Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences**
- Drop lower-priority or older-sounding items like **jQuery** unless required by target roles.
- If possible, align wording to recent impact areas from NACo: **Drupal modernization, platform integrations, structured workflows, AI search**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the **Technical + IT** section; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- **AI-enabled search experiences** already appears in Core Competencies, so consider shortening here to **AI search and discovery** or removing it from one section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and misses the strategic value implied by this topline category. For a senior CV, emphasize decision support and optimization outcomes over listing platforms alone.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability statement: “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than just products.
- Tighten and group items by function, e.g. “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” followed by “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger phrasing: “KPI and dashboard design” or “Executive/leadership reporting” instead of “KPI design” and “Leadership reporting.”
- If space allows, add an outcome-oriented qualifier: “analytics infrastructure for executive decision-making” or “insight generation and performance optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep this version strategic and let the Technical section hold the full tools list.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and several NACo role bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and operations-focused rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit
- Reframe toward leadership + delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the in-house studio achievement.
- Tighten “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Hybrid and virtual event delivery” for stronger execution language.
- If space allows, add scale/setting in one phrase: “Livestream and hybrid event delivery for advocacy, conference, and member programming.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase here.
- Tool-level detail like PTZ/studio operations is useful here, but don’t also repeat it in multiple work-experience bullets unless tied to a concrete outcome.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills. Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize depth/relevance rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling strength: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of a bare list: **Drupal site building/migration • WordPress administration • SharePoint publishing • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep the strongest platform first; Drupal should clearly anchor this section given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- If other technical items stay detailed, keep this one concise and platform-focused only.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one or making this the shorter platform-only version.
- Avoid repeating CMS modernization here since it already appears in Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Reorder by relevance/recency: JavaScript • HTML5/CSS3 • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery
- Consider tightening phrasing to show level/scope: Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) • API integrations • Tag management (GTM) • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions) • Legacy support (jQuery)
- If space allows elsewhere, add proof instead of more tools: e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, workflow automation, and lightweight serverless functions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap with “Workflow automation”; keep it here only if you want this section to skew more technical.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and frame around higher-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by relevance to recent work and group by function: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana | Slack • Microsoft Teams | Trello • Basecamp
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show application, e.g. “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier (workflow automation); Jira, Asana (project operations); Slack, Teams (cross-team coordination)”
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value/older tools if not used recently, especially Basecamp or Trello, to keep the list current and senior-level

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating those exact phrases here
- Collaboration tools like Slack/Teams may feel low-signal unless balanced by stronger automation/platform items first

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and avoid repeating email leadership already covered in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Email & Engagement Platforms:** Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add qualifiers to show depth: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation)** • **Higher Logic (member email/community communications)** • **Mailchimp (newsletter operations)**
- Prioritize the most relevant/current platform first; if Dynamics 365 is your strongest or most recent, keep it first and consider dropping Mailchimp if exposure was limited.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect one platform to scale or outcome rather than listing tools only.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and multi-channel communications; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- “Engagement” may blur with analytics/communications leadership already covered; “Platforms” is cleaner and more precise.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills almost exactly. Use this section for sharper technical specificity, not broad capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Google Tag Manager • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • Experimentation**
- Replace vague nouns like **A/B testing** and **Dashboarding** with stronger, more technical phrasing such as **Experimentation**, **KPI reporting**, or **Performance analysis**
- If accurate, add one higher-signal analytics implementation skill not listed elsewhere, e.g. **event tracking**, **conversion measurement**, **data visualization**, or **report automation**
- Keep the list tool-first and concise; reserve outcomes/impact for recent NACo roles where you already mention analytics infrastructure expansion

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one or making this version more tool-specific
- **SEO** is broad; if retained here, use **SEO analysis** to avoid sounding like a duplicate competency area

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” or scale achieved during this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add specific outputs or scale if available: website size/traffic at refresh, number/frequency of livestreams, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or production volume.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a sharper full version: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, support a major website refresh, and standardize publishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, while guiding a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Workflow/governance language also appears in later roles; keep this item focused on foundational team-building and production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and keep the media work concise.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and the standout result: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo program development and policy communications.”
- Tighten the media clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational campaigns and member-facing materials.”
- Keep the differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one concrete outcome: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or programs/policy teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership here; reserve team-building and enterprise digital ownership for 2015–2024 entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
